answer: Submitted in English per public benchmark contract. Single grounded hypothesis: among Black respondents (n=2,465 after dedup; 124 ever jailed), incarceration is associated with substantial wealth loss that is non-uniform across initial-wealth strata — amplified at the bottom and attenuated at the top. Quantitatively: median 1996 wealth collapses to $0 in T1/T2 (≈100% penalty) vs $7,250 vs $28,250 in T3 (−74%); mean asinh 1985→1996 growth shortfall attenuates monotonically from −5.60 (T1) → −3.33 (T2) → −2.57 (T3) asinh units. Quintiles downgraded to tertiles because Q2 x ever_jailed=1 had n=7 (cell-size guardrail); all tertile cells ≥38. Cross-race context (hispanic, white) shows qualitatively similar median collapse, with attenuation at the top tertile visible for Black (−74%) and white (−89%). Framed as associative/descriptive only (no causal claim): temporal overlap between ever_jailed (1985-1994 window) and point wealth measurements, plus absence of income/education/employment controls, preclude causal interpretation.

payload.hypothesis: Among Black respondents in this NLSY-processed sample (n=2,465 after dedup; 124 ever jailed 1985–1994), ever being jailed is associated with substantially lower wealth in 1996 across every initial-wealth stratum, and the wealth penalty is non-uniform — amplified at the bottom of the wealth distribution and attenuated at the top: jailed Black respondents in the lowest and middle 1985-wealth tertiles collapse to a median 1996 wealth of $0 (≈100% penalty relative to non-jailed peers), those in the highest tertile retain about a quarter (−74%), and the shortfall in 1985→1996 wealth accumulation (mean asinh-transformed growth) attenuates monotonically from −5.60 asinh units in the lowest tertile to −3.33 in the middle and −2.57 in the highest.
payload.workflow: Stage 1 — Clean: load nls_incarceration_processed.csv, normalize 'hipanic'→'hispanic', drop 1,899 full-row duplicates (12,013 → 10,114 rows). Stage 2 — Stratify: within Black subsample, compute tertile cut-points of composite_wealth_1985 (USD 20, 5,508); documented downgrade from quintiles because Q2 × ever_jailed=1 had n=7 (<30 threshold); all tertile cells ≥38. Stage 3 — Headline: report medians of W1985/W1990/W1996, median W1996 penalty (j1−j0), and mean asinh growth 1985→1996 penalty by tertile × ever_jailed. Stage 4 — Secondary: sex-disaggregated medians (reported only as secondary per guardrail, since female-T3 cell is small) and cross-race context (own-race tertile breakpoints). All outputs associative/descriptive; no causal language.
